title: Practice: Binary Search
prompt: Trace the Python 3.12+ example in lesson 46, “Binary Search”. Which option exactly matches its standard output? For multiple lines, the symbol ⏎ represents a newline.
objective: Practice the main ideas in Binary Search.
target_skills: Relate the example to the lesson concept
Recognize a common failure or output mismatch

options: The snippet raises an exception before producing the expected output.

acceptance_criteria: Select the exact stdout shown by the code when run locally.
Be able to trace the relevant variable or data-structure changes.
Explain why one plausible distractor differs.
hints: Read each statement in order and update variables manually.
Remember that print() displays values, while assignments and method calls may not print.
Pay attention to collection order, quotes, and newline boundaries.
grading_method: Server-side single-choice comparison of the traced output. No learner code is executed; this checks code-reading/output tracing, not the correctness of a separate implementation.
retry_policy: Allow retries after reviewing feedback; platform-wide XP rules control rewards and no per-exercise XP override is authored.
status_note: Single-choice output-trace exercise generated from this lesson’s local, verified Python example. Draft until instructional review.
